samples.summary: Importing a *default* (non-`--raw`) `sheets export` CSV writes the neutralized text `'=SUM(...)` into the cell's **formula** field
samples.evidence: `sheets export` without `--raw` runs `formatCsv(res.data, { neutralizeFormulas: true })` (sheets-export.ts:63), which prefixes the `formula` column with `'` (csv.ts:41). The header row `ref,value,formula[,style]` is unaffected by neutralization, so `isCellTable()` (csv-parse.ts:103) still matches and `buildCellMapFromTable` takes the `formula` branch: `if (formula !== '') cells[ref] = { formula }` — sending `{ formula: "'=SUM(B2:B100)" }` to the batch API. Nothing anywhere strips the guard quote on the way back in, so the round trip the skills docs describe (`export out.csv` then `import out.csv`, and the pre-existing recipe in recipe-csv-pipeline.md which does exactly that) now silently writes a malformed formula into every formula cell of the target document. Before this change the same file imported as an obviously-wrong positional grid and never touched the formula field. Either strip a single leading `'` in `buildCellMapFromTable`, or refuse a table whose formula column is quoted.

samples.summary: `buildCellMap` silently changes the meaning of every existing positional CSV import: a cell whose text starts with `=` is now sent as a formula, not a value
samples.evidence: `buildCellMap` previously produced `{ value }` unconditionally; it now routes through `toCellPatch` (csv-parse.ts:90-92), which returns `{ formula: text }` for any `text.startsWith('=')`. This is the generic `sheets import <doc> data.csv` path, not just the export round trip, and it is a behavior change for every user/script importing a CSV that contains literal `=`-leading text (e.g. `=TBD`, `=>`, `=1+1` meant as a label). Such a value now becomes a live formula — and an unparseable one may make the whole `PATCH .../cells` batch fail, breaking an import that previously succeeded. No opt-out flag exists on the import side (only `--raw` on export), so there is no way to get the old literal-text behavior back.

samples.summary: `isCellTable` header heuristic hijacks any ordinary CSV whose first three columns are named ref/value/formula, silently ignoring `--start` and mis-placing the data
samples.evidence: `isCellTable` (csv-parse.ts:103-107) matches on nothing but the first three header cells being `ref`,`value`,`formula` (case/space-insensitive). A user's own domain CSV with those perfectly ordinary column names is now imported by reference: the header row is dropped, `--start` is silently ignored (sheets-import.ts:104-107), rows whose first column is not a cell ref are dropped entirely (`continue` at csv-parse.ts:120), and everything else lands at whatever ref the file's first column happens to spell. That is silent data loss / misplacement relative to the documented positional-grid behavior. The `mode` field in the response is the only signal, and it is emitted after the write has already happened.

samples.summary: The callback can mint a CLI redirect with no `state`, which the new CLI unconditionally refuses — the code is burned and `wafflebase login` hangs for the full 3-minute timeout
samples.evidence: `const stateParam = state.nonce ? ... : ''` makes the echoed nonce optional server-side, but the CLI's loopback server treats a missing `state` as fatal: `if (!nonceMatches(nonce, state)) { refuse(...); return; }` (login.ts:320-328) and a refusal deliberately never settles the wait. So whenever `state.nonce` is undefined the server mints a real code for the user's account (spending the one-shot CLI state), redirects to `127.0.0.1:<port>/callback?code=...` with no `state`, and the CLI refuses it and blocks until `CALLBACK_TIMEOUT_MS`. This is reachable whenever the nonce fails `parseCliNonce` (github-auth.guard.ts:18-21) while the challenge passes — the guard stores `undefined` for the nonce but still mints the state, and the challenge check at auth.controller.ts:196 passes. The two halves disagree about whether the nonce is optional; the backend should refuse to mint a code for a nonce-less CLI state exactly as it refuses a challenge-less one.

samples.summary: `--raw` export → import is still not an identity: an exported literal cell whose *text* starts with `=` comes back as a formula
samples.evidence: In `buildCellMapFromTable`, a row with an empty formula column falls to `cells[ref] = toCellPatch(value)` (line 129), which promotes any `value` starting with `=` to `{ formula }`. Under `--raw` a cell holding the literal text `=TBD` (no formula) is written verbatim into the value column and re-imports as a formula. The `--raw` round trip is documented in skills/sheets-import-export.md as the identity path; for literal `=` text it is not. Using `{ value }` unconditionally in the table path (the `ref` table already distinguishes the two columns) would fix it.

samples.summary: The `Missing code` 400 branch does not record `lastRefusal`, so that failure never reaches the timeout message
samples.evidence: Every other rejection path funnels through `refuse()` which sets `lastRefusal` (login.ts:280-289) and is then reported by `loginTimeoutMessage`. The `if (!code) { res.writeHead(400); res.end('Missing code'); return; }` branch at lines 313-317 writes the response directly and leaves `lastRefusal` untouched, so a callback arriving with no `code` (e.g. GitHub/backend error redirect) hangs the login for three minutes and then reports the bare 'Login timed out.' with no cause — the exact silent-hang failure mode the rest of this change was written to remove.

samples.summary: `loginErrorUrl` emits a same-origin relative redirect when `FRONTEND_URL` is unset, landing the user on a backend 404
samples.evidence: `const frontend = (this.configService.get<string>('FRONTEND_URL') ?? '').replace(/\/+$/, '')` yields `''`, so the redirect target becomes `/login?error=oauth_state` — a relative URL that `res.redirect` resolves against the *backend* origin, which has no `/login` route. The whole stated point of redirecting instead of throwing is to land the user on a page they can retry from; the fallback defeats it. The existing web-success path uses `this.configService.get('FRONTEND_URL')!` (line 228), i.e. it treats the value as required — this new helper quietly tolerates its absence and produces a broken URL instead.

samples.summary: `cells batch` dry-run block was moved outside the try/catch, so a throw from `getConfig`/`printDryRun` now escapes the error envelope
samples.evidence: The dry-run branch (`if (opts.dryRun) { printDryRun(getConfig(opts), ...); return; }`, lines 147-155) used to sit inside the `try` whose `catch` called `outputError`. It is now bare between two try blocks. Any throw from `getConfig` (which reads and YAML-parses the config file via `resolveConfig`) or `printDryRun` rejects the action promise instead of producing the documented `{ error: { code, message } }` envelope with exit 1 — the same class of regression the surrounding comment says it is fixing for JSON parsing.

samples.summary: `--raw` is silently ignored for a JSON export rather than rejected
samples.evidence: `const formatted = fmt === 'csv' ? formatCsv(res.data, { neutralizeFormulas: !localOpts.raw }) : formatJson(res.data)` — passing `--raw` with `--file-format json` (or a `.json` filename) is accepted and has no effect. The flag help says 'CSV only', but nothing enforces it, so a caller who believes `--raw` is what makes the round trip faithful gets no signal that it did nothing.

samples.summary: An expired/cross-browser CLI state throws raw backend JSON while the *same* class of failure on the web path was deliberately turned into a friendly redirect
samples.evidence: The web branch redirects to `loginErrorUrl('oauth_state')` precisely because a state cookie expiring or being overwritten by a second tab is 'reachable without any attacker' (comment at lines 134-141). The CLI branch has the identical no-attacker failure modes — the `wafflebase_cli_state` cookie is five minutes and a second `wafflebase login` in another tab overwrites it (both cookies use `path: '/'` and a fixed name) — yet it still throws `BadRequestException`, leaving the user on the backend origin looking at JSON. Worse, the CLI process is simultaneously blocked in `waitForCallback()` and gets no callback at all, so it hangs for the full three-minute timeout with the generic message.

verdict.reason: Code is exactly as described. sheets-export.ts:63 neutralizes by default via formatCsv({neutralizeFormulas: !raw}); csv.ts:33-42+91 prefixes the per-field `formula` column with `'` (header keys ref/value/formula/style are not formula triggers so the header survives intact); csv-parse.ts:103-107 isCellTable therefore still matches a neutralized export; csv-parse.ts:126-127 unconditionally sends `{ formula }` with no leading-quote stripping, and sheets-import.ts:105-118 passes it straight to batchCells (http-client.ts:356-362, no sanitization). I found no guard on any path that strips or rejects a `'`-quoted formula, so a default export re-imported writes the malformed formula `'=SUM(...)` into every formula cell. The skills docs (sheets-import-export.md:110-119) advise `--raw` but that is documentation, not a code guard, and they even misdescribe the result as landing as literal text (it lands in the formula field). Real, in-lane data-corruption bug.

verdict.reason: Code is present exactly as described. `toCellPatch` (csv-parse.ts:90-92) returns `{formula: text}` for any `=`-leading text, and `buildCellMap` — the positional-grid builder used by the generic `sheets import` path (sheets-import.ts:103-107, chosen whenever `isCellTable` is false) — now routes every cell through it (csv-parse.ts:149). The repo's own task notes confirm the prior behavior was `{ value }` only (docs/tasks/active/20260806-...-todo.md:283-287). There is no import-side opt-out (sheets-import.ts:44-50 has only --tab/--file-format/--start; --raw is export-only, sheets-export.ts:30-34); the only escape is per-cell `'` prefixing, which alters the stored text (test csv-parse.test.ts:113-120). Impact is real: the backend sets `f: cellData.formula` and `v: cellData.value ?? existing?.v ?? ''` (cells.controller.ts:168-172), so literal text like `=TBD` becomes a live formula with a blanked/stale value — silent data reinterpretation on a path that previously stored it verbatim. I could not substantiate one sub-claim (that an unparseable formula fails the whole PATCH batch): the backend stores `f` without parsing. That weakens part of the evidence but not the core defect, so the finding stands rather than being refuted.

verdict.reason: Verified in the repository; the code matches the finding line-for-line. `isCellTable` (csv-parse.ts:103-107) keys the entire import mode off nothing but the first three header cells equalling ref/value/formula after trim+lowercase — no column-count check, no sampling of data rows, no provenance marker. When it fires, `buildCellMapFromTable` (csv-parse.ts:114-133) drops the header row and silently `continue`s past every row whose first column fails /^[A-Z]+\d+$/ (csv-parse.ts:120), so an ordinary domain CSV with those column names either imports nothing or lands data at whatever refs its first column happens to spell. `--start` is parsed at sheets-import.ts:104 but consumed only by the grid branch (sheets-import.ts:105-107), so it is silently inert, and there is no --mode/--as-grid override among the command options (sheets-import.ts:44-50). The `mode` signal is built at sheets-import.ts:109 and returned at sheets-import.ts:120-122, i.e. after the write at sheets-import.ts:118, and is absent from the dry-run path (sheets-import.ts:111-116). No guard or caller elsewhere narrows the heuristic, so the silent misplacement/data-loss path is genuinely reachable — squarely a correctness-lane defect. No refutation ground applies.

verdict.reason: The code is present exactly as described. auth.controller.ts:207-209 makes the echoed nonce optional (`state.nonce ? '&state=...' : ''`) while minting a real code at :202 and having already spent the one-shot state at :184 (cli-auth.store.ts:96-97 deletes the entry unconditionally). The CLI's loopback server treats a missing `state` as fatal (login.ts:319-328, nonceMatches returns false for null at :198) and a refusal never settles the wait, so the promise only resolves via the 180s timer (login.ts:212, 397-403) — a burned code plus a blocked login. The nonce-less state is genuinely constructible: github-auth.guard.ts:82 feeds parseCliNonce's `undefined` (guard.ts:18-21) into createState's optional `nonce?` (cli-auth.store.ts:53-71), consumeState returns it as-is (:107-112), and cli-login-confirm.middleware.ts:76-82,113,134-136 requires only `port`, so a malformed/duplicated `nonce` still passes the confirm gate and the challenge check at auth.controller.ts:196. The asymmetry the reviewer names is real: :196-201 refuses a challenge-less CLI state but nothing refuses a nonce-less one, and auth.controller.spec.ts:251-271 asserts the permissive behavior. No guard makes the path unreachable; the shipped CLI always sending a valid 64-hex nonce (login.ts:34,46,168-170) narrows the trigger but is not a guard. Only minor inaccuracy: the CLI does print the refusal reason immediately (login.ts:286), so the hang is diagnosable rather than silent — this does not change the defect. Falls squarely in the correctness lane (broken cross-component invariant / mis-handled failure breaking the login flow), so no refutation ground applies.
